title: EnCAgg: Enhanced Clustering Aggregation for Robust Federated Learning against Dynamic Model Poisoning

C-a.quote: shows the framework of our method, which consists of three main parts: • Distance-based Low-dimensional Gradient Clustering: The server computes pairwise differences among gradients submitted by clients to identify the two most variant dimensions, projecting gradients into a low-dimensional space to enhance separability between benign and malicious gradients. Density-based clustering then splits lowdimensional gradients into clusters, while server applies filter algorithm to exclude possible malicious gradients and retain others for next steps.
C-a.locator: §IV-A Overview; the count reaches two under the GRANULARITY RULE (row 45) and the generator is excised under AMENDMENT 3. (1) FIRST-PASS density-based clustering with the filter algorithm: the purpose is in the quoted bullet, "applies filter algorithm to exclude possible malicious gradients", restated in the Abstract as "First, we introduce a density-based low-dimensional gradient clustering method, which projects gradients onto the two most divergent dimensions and applies density-based clustering to identify malicious gradients while retaining clustered benign gradients and potentially benign outliers.". (2) RE-CLUSTERING is a SECOND, INDEPENDENT DECISION over the retained set, not a stage in computing the first signal: "• Low-dimensional Gradient Re-Clustering: Retained real gradients and pseudo-gradients are combined for a second clustering. Sparse benign gradients can now join the benign cluster via the bridges built by pseudo-gradient, while distant noise points, which are more likely malicious now, are excluded. Only high-dimensional gradients corresponding to the real gradients in final benign cluster are aggregated, while pseudo-gradients are excluded." -- it emits its own verdict on a different input (real plus pseudo gradients) with its own exclusion criterion, and the paper states that criterion's basis, "Since inter-class distances (benign vs. malicious) typically exceed intra-class variation, gradients still labeled as noise are likely adversarial and safely removed.". Under the row-45 rule (distinct iff it contributes an independent discriminative signal or an independent decision) that is two. (3) THE GENERATOR IS EXCLUDED: its stated purpose for inclusion is recovering wrongly excluded benign gradients, not resisting poisoned updates -- "• Enhancing-Clustering Low-dimensional Gradient Generation: A generator model produces pseudo-gradients near the benign cluster boundary, linking it to sparsely located benign gradients previously misclassified as noise, thereby improving their likelihood of being correctly clustered in the next stage." and "Third, we introduce low-dimensional gradient re-clustering that clusters the generated pseudo-gradients together with real gradients to recover benign gradients misclassified as noise points, enabling more benign gradients to participate in aggregation.". SEVENTH INSTANCE OF THE EXCISED-CONSTITUENT PATTERN and a new purpose kind (fidelity / benign retention). C-a does NOT depend on the generator: it is YES on the two clustering decisions alone

C-b.quote: Since PCA directions depend on dominant distributions, the relative positions of benign and malicious gradients can shift unpredictably between rounds when benign and malicious ratio are similar, hindering consistent boundary learning. After filtering most malicious gradients, reapplying PCA yields more stable projections, helping the generator better capture the benign cluster’s g
C-b.locator: §IV-C; THIS IS A CONSTITUENT-PROPERTY REASON OF AN UNUSUAL AND, FOR THIS AUDIT, UNUSUALLY VALUABLE KIND: the reason for placing the generator after the first filter is that the filter CHANGES THE DISTRIBUTION the generator's projection is estimated from, and the paper gives the mechanism (PCA directions depend on the dominant distribution, so with a similar benign/malicious ratio the geometry shifts unpredictably between rounds). The first constituent's standalone effect is what makes the second work, which is the standalone-effectiveness limb of C-b. The same reason is stated as a reliability claim at §IV-B, "Notably, even if strong attacks cause some benign gradients to be marked as noise, the geometric optimization strategy still helps identify the most likely benign cluster, providing a reliable foundation for the next-stage processing.", and at §IV-B's radius selection, "This conservative selection improves the quality of clustering and provides a secure basis for subsequent steps.". The complementary-threat-coverage limb is present too, against PRIOR families rather than its own constituents: "However, when no malicious gradients are present in an iteration, forced clustering may wrongly discard benign gradients. Besides, if malicious clients are dominant, they may form the largest cluster and evade detection." and "However, benign updates may be inherently scattered and appear as outliers, while well-crafted malicious updates may form dense clusters that are mistakenly trusted as benign.". The residual-coverage version of the pairing, in the threat direction, is "Since inter-class distances (benign vs. malicious) typically exceed intra-class variation, gradients still labeled as noise are likely adversarial and safely removed." -- the first pass deliberately RETAINS potentially-benign outliers and the second pass is what removes the malicious ones among them

C-c.quote: 2) Robustness Evaluation: Table III and Table IV report the performance of all methods on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and MIND.
C-c.locator: §VI; the metric is ROBUST ACCURACY of the assembled framework -- "TABLE III ROBUSTNESS E VALUATION ON MNIST AND CIFAR10 ( ACCURACY (%) )" -- reported against FedSGD, Krum, Median, Trimmed Mean, FLTrust, DPFLA and FLGuardian under UA-FedRec, LIE and Min-Max at 10% and 60% malicious clients on MNIST, CIFAR-10 and MIND (AUC/MRR/nDCG for the MIND recommendation task, Table IV), plus a paper-designed adaptive attack in Table V. There is no ASR and no backdoor metric in this paper (3 occurrences of "backdoor", 0 of "ASR"), so the code rests on the robust-accuracy limb, as with BROADCAST, DP-BREM, BRFL and DDFed. The composed outcome is read mechanistically at §VI, "However, EnCAgg overcomes this by blocking such perturbations from entering the benign cluster through carefully designed clustering and maintaining robustness."

C-d.quote: Removing dimensionality reduction causes a larger performance drop of approximately 0.7. Dimensionality reduction improves the separability between benign and malicious gradients. Without it, attackers can more easily craft gradients within the clustering radius, bypassing the filtering mechanism and degrading model performance.
C-d.locator: §VI-6 Ablation Study, Fig. 6; FOUR ARMS, and the extracted arm labels are "Method PCA+Clust+Gen PCA+Clust Clust+Gen Clust 65.00 13 36 64.50 34 64.25 64.00 32 63.75 63.50 30 AUC MRR nDCG@5 nDCG@10" -- PCA+Clust+Gen (full), PCA+Clust (no generator), Clust+Gen (no projection), Clust (neither) -- on MIND with 10% malicious clients running UA-FedRec, so the attack is held fixed. THE ARM THAT CARRIES THE CODE IS Clust+Gen: it removes the PROJECTION, the most upstream stage, while the density-based clustering, the generator and the re-clustering downstream are unchanged, and the paper reads the outcome off what the FIXED DOWNSTREAM FILTER can then do -- "Without it, attackers can more easily craft gradients within the clustering radius, bypassing the filtering mechanism and degrading model performance." That is an explicit statement of a downstream mechanism's dependence on its input, which is the object of Prop. prop:identification_full. A SECOND ARM RUNS THE SAME DIRECTION: PCA+Clust removes the generator, which sits upstream of the re-clustering, holding the re-clustering fixed -- "As shown in Fig. 6, removing the generator causes an approximately 0.1 performance drop. This is because pseudo-gradients help pull sparsely distributed benign updates into the benign cluster during the second round of clustering. Without them, these updates are treated as noise and excluded from aggregation, resulting in incomplete global updates.". Full ablation passage: "6) Ablation Study: Finally, we conduct ablation studies on the MIND dataset with 10% malicious clients performing UA-FedRec attacks to evaluate the contributions of dimensionality reduction and the gradient generator. As shown in Fig. 6, removing the generator causes an approximately 0.1 performance drop. This is because pseudo-gradients help pull sparsely distributed benign updates into the benign cluster during the second round of clustering. Without them, these updates are treated as noise and excluded from aggregation, resulting in incomplete global updates. Removing dimensionality reduction causes a larger performance drop of approximately 0.7. Dimensionality reduction improves the separability between benign and malicious gradients. Without it, attackers can more easily craft gradients within the clustering radius, bypassing the filtering mechanism and degrading model performance. When both components are removed, the performance drops by approximately 1.3, indicating that density-based clustering alone is insufficient for robust defense. The results demonstrate that dimensionality reduction and pseudo-gradient generation jointly contribute to the effectiveness of EnCAgg.". Neither arm removes a downstream stage, so unlike FedSAC, SecureAFL and FedSurrogate this table contains NO arm in the declined direction. Rule 4 is not needed. A knob sweep is NOT available as a second route: the paper reports single values for r, min_samples, \u03b3 and n_gen in Table I and sweeps none of them; Figs. 4 and 5 vary the MALICIOUS CLIENT RATIO, which is the attack, and so cannot hold it fixed

C-e.quote: When both components are removed, the performance drops by approximately 1.3, indicating that density-based clustering alone is insufficient for robust defense.
C-e.locator: §VI-6; the claim names a constituent (density-based clustering) and says what it does NOT contribute on its own to the combined result. Three further constituent-level attributions: "As shown in Fig. 6, removing the generator causes an approximately 0.1 performance drop. This is because pseudo-gradients help pull sparsely distributed benign updates into the benign cluster during the second round of clustering. Without them, these updates are treated as noise and excluded from aggregation, resulting in incomplete global updates." (the generator), "Removing dimensionality reduction causes a larger performance drop of approximately 0.7. Dimensionality reduction improves the separability between benign and malicious gradients. Without it, attackers can more easily craft gradients within the clustering radius, bypassing the filtering mechanism and degrading model performance." (the projection), and the mechanism statement at §IV-D, "r boundary effectively expands its ε-neighborhood, shortening the distance to sparsely distributed benign gradients and increasing their inclusion likelihood." coder_note:
DESIGN = YES, PRIMARY = NO, AND THIS ROW IS THE FRAME'S CLOSEST EXTERNAL ANALOGUE TO OUR OWN PROPOSITION -- CLOSER THAN ANY OF THE SIX COMPOSITION-INVARIANCE TREATMENTS A3 HAS BEEN ASSEMBLING. Every one of those six treats the question as: does inserting an upstream transform leave a downstream guarantee, decision or detector unchanged? Four answer by proof (Fed-DPRoC, SRFed Thm 6.2, CQSA, Byz-Clip21-SGD2M -- the last with the opposite sign), two by measurement (DDFed, SecureAFL). EnCAgg does something none of them does: it (i) states a MECHANISM for why the downstream stage's behaviour depends on what the upstream filter removed -- PCA directions track the dominant distribution, so the projected geometry moves between rounds when the benign/malicious ratio is near parity -- (ii) CHANGES THE DESIGN in response, re-applying PCA to the filtered set rather than the raw set, and (iii) MEASURES the dependence in an ablation arm that removes the upstream stage and holds the downstream fixed. Articulate, act, measure. A3 should present EnCAgg as the closest external precedent and then say precisely what our contribution adds to it, because a reviewer who finds this paper and thinks we did not will read the omission as the novelty problem the nineteenth review already flagged. Concretely: EnCAgg establishes the dependence for ONE upstream/downstream pair inside its own pipeline as a design justification; it does not treat the dependence as the object of study, does not vary the upstream stage across a graded family at fixed downstream, and reads a single scalar (a ~0.7 drop) rather than an ordering across upstream strengths.

C-a = 2, AND THE GRANULARITY RULE IS WHAT MAKES IT SO. The pipeline runs density-based clustering TWICE, and a coarse reading -- "one clustering mechanism, applied twice" -- would give C-a = NO and take this row out of DESIGN. I applied the row-45 rule as frozen in the SRFed record: distinct iff the component contributes an independent discriminative signal or an independent DECISION, and not when it is a stage in computing one signal. The two passes emit two verdicts on two different point sets under two different criteria: the first excludes what is far from the dense benign cluster while DELIBERATELY RETAINING outliers that might be benign, and the second, over an augmented point set, excludes what is still isolated after the bridges are built, on the stated basis that inter-class distance exceeds intra-class variation. Two decisions, so two. THE DIRECTION OF THIS JUDGMENT FAVOURS OUR THESIS (it puts a paper into DESIGN), which is why the alternative reading is written out here rather than left implicit; and it does not reach the primary either way, because C-d = YES independently on two arms.

SEVENTH EXCISED CONSTITUENT, AND THE FIRST WHOSE PURPOSE IS TO REPAIR THE DEFENSE'S OWN COLLATERAL DAMAGE. The excised purposes across the frame are now fairness/inclusion (PPFA-BA), encryption (SecureDyn-FL), secure aggregation (CQSA), temporal stability + communication + heterogeneity (FedEMA-Distill), privacy-sensitivity clipping + variance reduction (Byz-Clip21-SGD2M), asynchrony/partial participation (SecureAFL), and now FIDELITY / BENIGN RETENTION (this row). The last is a genuinely different sub-kind and A5 should say so: the generator does not defend against anything, it recovers benign gradients the first filter wrongly discarded, so under Amendment 3's text -- purpose must be to resist faulty, malicious or poisoned updates -- it is out. A reader could object that reducing a defense's false-positive rate IS part of defending. I record the objection rather than pre-empting it, and note that FedSurrogate's Stage 2 (2605.11122) was counted IN on the same territory because its stated purpose is BIDIRECTIONAL -- it demotes residual adversaries as well as rescuing false positives -- whereas EnCAgg's generator is stated only in the rescue direction. That pair is the sharpest illustration in the frame of where Amendment 3's line actually falls, and A5 must present them together.

THE ABLATION HAS NO ARM IN THE DECLINED DIRECTION, WHICH MAKES IT UNUSUAL. FedSAC, SecureAFL and FedSurrogate each ran one arm each way and the coder had to sort them. Here both arms remove UPSTREAM stages while the downstream survives, so the whole table is identifying. That is worth a sentence in A5 as the counter-example to the claim that ablation tables are systematically pointed the wrong way: they are not systematically anything, and the rubric's direction test has to be applied arm by arm.

NOTE ON WHAT THE ABLATION IS SMALL. The effects are ~0.1 (generator), ~0.7 (projection) and ~1.3 (both) on MIND's ranking metrics at 10% malicious clients, on one dataset and one attack. The code does not depend on effect size -- C-d asks whether the contrast was run, not whether it was decisive -- but A4 should not present EnCAgg as a well-powered measurement of the interaction, because a single-dataset, single-attack, single-ratio, no-repetition arm is not one. This is the honest version of the claim: the contrast exists and is read, at a scale that could not order upstream strengths.
